ἄλλος.long: other, another (of more than two), different.
ἄλλος.as:
ἄλλος, -η, -ο, (cf. Lat. alius, Eng. else),
[in LXX for אַחֵר ,אֶחָד, etc.;]
other, another: absol., Mt 20:3, al.; ἄ. δέ, I Co 3:1012:8; pl., Mk 6:15; attached to a noun, Mt 2:124:21, al.; c. art., ὁ ἄ., the other, Mt 5:39, Jo 19:32 (Bl., §47, 8); οἱ ἄ., the others, the rest, Jo 20:25, I Co 14:29; ἄ. πρὸς ἄλλον = πρὸς ἀλλήλους (BL, §48, 10), Ac 2:12; ἄλλ’ (i.e. ἄλλο) ἤ (Bl., §77, 13), Lk 12:51; seq. πλήν, Mk 12:32; εἰ μή, Jo 6:22; παρά c. acc., I Co 3:11.
SYN.: ἕτερος, q.v. ἄ. denotes numerical, ἕ. qualitative difference (Cremer, 89). ἄ. generally "denotes simply distinction of individuals, ἕ. involves the secondary idea of difference in kind" (v. Lft., Meyer, Ramsay, on Ga 1:6, 7; Tr., Syn., §xcv; Bl., §51, 6; M, Pr., 79f., 246; MM, VGT, s.vv.). As to whether the distinction can be maintained in I Co 12:8, 10 v. ICC, in l., and on He 11:35f., v. Westc, in l.

ἅλων.sd: a threshing-floor (as rolled hard), i.e. (figuratively) the grain (and chaff, as just threshed)
ἅλων.der: probably from the base of G1507 (εἱλίσσω);
ἅλων.as:
ἅλων, -ωνος
(for Attic ἅλως, -ω, v. MM, VGT, s.v.), ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for גֹּרֶן;]
a threshing floor: Mt 3:12, Lk 3:17 (here prob. by meton. = the grain on the threshing floor).†

ἀλλά.sd: properly, other things, i.e. (adverbially) contrariwise (in many relations)
ἀλλά.kj: and, but (even), howbeit, indeed, nay, nevertheless, no, notwithstanding, save, therefore, yea, yet
ἀλλά.as:
ἀλλά (ἀλλ’ usually bef. α and υ, often bef. ε and η, rarely bef. ο and ω, never bef. ι; Tdf., Pr., 93 f.; WH, App., 146),
adversative particle,
stronger than δέ; prop. neuter pl. of ἄλλος, used adverbially, with changed accent; hence prop. otherwise, on the other hand (cf. Ro 3:31);
1. opposing a previous negation, but: οὐ (μὴ) . . . ἀ., Mt 5:15, 17Mk 5:39, Jo 7:16, al.; rhetorically subordinating but not entirely negativing what precedes, οὐ . . . ἀ., not so much . . . as, Mk 9:37, Mt 10:20, Jo 12:44, al.; with ellipse of the negation, Mt 11:7-9, Ac 19:2, I Co 3:66:11 7:7, II Co 7:1, Ga 2:3, al.; in opposition to a foregoing pos. sentence, ἀ. οὐ, Mt 24:6, I Co 10:23; οὐ μόνον . . . ἀ. καί, Jo 5:18, Ro 1:32, al.; elliptically, after a negation, ἀ. ἵνα, Mk 14:49, Jo 1:89:3, al.; = εἰ μή (Bl., §77, 13; M, Pr., 241; but cf. WM, §iii, 10), Mt 20:23, Mk 4:22.
2. Without previous negation, to express opposition, interruption, transition, etc., but: Jo 16:2012:27, Ga 2:14; before commands or requests, Ac 10:2026:16, Mt 9:18, Mk 9:22, al.; to introduce an accessory idea, II Co 7:11; in the apodosis after a condition or concession with εἰ, ἐάν, εἴπερ, yet, still, at least, Mk 14:29, I Co 9:2, II Co 4:16, Col 2:5, al.; after μέν, Ac 4:17, Ro 14:20, I Co 14:17; giving emphasis to the following clause, ἀλλ’ ἔρχεται ὥρα, yea, etc., Jo 16:2; so with neg., ἀλλ’ οὐδέ, nay, nor yet, Lk 23:15.
3. Joined with other particles (a practice which increases in late writers; Simcox, LNT, 166), ἀ. γε, yet at least, Lk 24:21, I Co 9:2; ἄ ἤ., save only, except, Lk 12:51, II Co 1:13; ἀ. μὲν οὖν, Phl 3:8 (on this usage, v. MM, VGT, s.v.).

ἁλιεύς.sd: a sailor (as engaged on the salt water), i.e. (by implication) a fisher

ἅλας.as:
ἅλας (T, ἅλα), -ατος, τό, late form of cl. ἅλς, -ος, ὁ (MM, VGT, s.v.),
[in LXX chiefly for מְלַח ;]
salt, lit, and fig.: Mt 5:13, Mk 9:50Lk 14:34; like cl. ἅλες, wit, of wisdom and grace in speech: Col 4:6.†

ἁλίζω.g: I salt, sprinkle with salt, keep fresh and sound
ἁλίζω.long: I salt, sprinkle with salt (of sacrifices or of those who offer sacrifice), keep fresh and sound, and so acceptable to God.
ἁλίζω.as:
ἁλίζω
(< ἅλς), [in LXX for מָלַח;]
to salt, season with salt: Mt 5:13, Mk 9:49.†

ἀλείφω.long: I anoint: festivally, in homage, medicinally, or in anointing the dead.
ἀλείφω.der: from G1 (Α) (as particle of union) and the base of G3045 (λιπαρός);
ἀλείφω.as:
ἀλείφω
(cf. λίπος, oil), [in LXX: Ge 31:13, Ex 40:15, Nu 3:3 (משׁח), Ez 13:10 ff. (טוח), Ru 3:3, II Ki 12:2014:2, IV Ki 4:2, II Ch 28:15, Mi 6:15, Da LXX TH 10:3 (סוךְ), Es 2:12, Jth 16:8*;]
to anoint, festally or in homage: c. acc rei or pers., Mt 6:17, Jo 12:3, Mk 16:1; seq. dat., ἐλαίῳ, Mk 6:13, Ja 5:14; μύρῳ, Lk 7:38, 46, Jo 11:2.†
SYN.: χρίω, μυρίζω (against the distinction made bet. ἀ. and χ. in Tr., Syn., § 38, v. MM, VGT, s.v., ἀ.)

ἀλώπηξ.long: a fox; a fox-like, crafty person.
ἀλώπηξ.sd: a fox, i.e. (figuratively) a cunning person
ἀλώπηξ.as:
ἀλώπηξ, -εκος, ἡ,
[in LXX for שׁוּעָל;]
a fox: Mt 8:20, Lk 9:58; metaph., of Herod, Lk 13:32.†

Ἁλφαῖος.long: Alphaeus; apparently two persons, (a) father of Levi, and (b) father of James.
Ἁλφαῖος.as:
Ἀλφαῖος (WH, Ἀλ-), -ου, ὁ (Aram. חַלְפַּי)
Alphæus.
1. Father of Levi: Mk 2:14.
2. Father of James: Mt 10:3, Mk 3:13, Lk 6:15, Ac 1:13.†

ἄλευρον.as:
ἄλευρον, -ου, τό
(< ἀλεύω, to grind), [in LXX for קֶמַח, Nu 5:15, al.;]
real: Mt 13:33, Lk 13:21.†

ἀληθῶς.kj: indeed, surely, of a surety, truly, of a (in) truth, verily, very
ἀληθῶς.as:
ἀληθῶς
adv.
(< ἀληθής), [in LXX (Je 28:6, Ps 58:1, al.) chiefly for אָמֵן and cogn. forms;]
truly, surely: Mt 14:3326:73Mk 14:7015:39, Lk 9:2712:4421:3, Jo 1:484:426:147:26, 408:3117:8Ac 12:11, I Th 2:13, I Jo 2:5.†

ἀλλότριος.long: belonging to another person, belonging to others, foreign, strange.
ἀλλότριος.sd: another's, i.e. not one's own; by extension foreign, not akin, hostile
ἀλλότριος.as:
ἀλλότριος, -α, -ον
(< ἄλλος), [in LXX for זוּר, נֵכָר, אַחֵר;]
1.belonging to another, not one's own (opp. to ἴδιος): Lk 16:12, Ro 14:415:20 (Field, Notes, 165 f.), II Co 10:15, 16, I Ti 5:22, He 9:25.
2.foreign, strange, alien (opp. to οἰκεῖος; v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 17:25, 26, Jo 10:5, Ac 7:6, He 11:9, 34.†

ἀληθής.long: unconcealed, true, true in fact, worthy of credit, truthful.
ἀληθής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2990 (λανθάνω);
ἀληθής.as:
ἀληθής, -ές
(< λήθω = λανθάνω, hence primarily, unconcealed, manifest; hence, actual, real), [in LXX for אֶמֶת, etc.;]
(a) of things, true, conforming to reality: Jo 4:185:31,326:55 (= ἀληθινός, q.v.) Jo 8:13,14, 1710:4119:3521:24, Ac 12:9, Phl 4:8, Tit 1:13, I Pe 5:12, II Pe 2:22, I Jo 2:8, III Jo 12;
(b) of persons, truthful: Mt 22:16, Mk 12:14, Jo 3:337:188:26, Ro 3:4, II Co 6:8.†
SYN.: ἀληθινός, real, genuine, ideal, as opp. to spurious or imperfect ἀληθής, true to fact, as opp. to false, lying, denotes the actuality of a thing: ἀληθινός, its relation to the corresponding conception. (Cf. Tr., Syn., § viii; Cremer, 84 f., 631 Abbott, JV, 234 f.; DB, iv, 818 f.; MM, VGT, s.vv.)

ἀλήθεια.long: truth, but not merely truth as spoken; truth of idea, reality, sincerity, truth in the moral sphere, divine truth revealed to man, straightforwardness.
ἀλήθεια.as:
ἀλήθεια, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀληθής), [in LXX chiefly for אֱמֶת (on which, v. Cremer, 627f.), אֱמוּנָה;]
truth (v. DB, iv, 818f.).
1. Objectively, "the reality lying at the basis of an appearance; the manifested, veritable essence of a matter" (Cremer, 86): Ro 9:1, al.; of religious truth, Ro 1:25, al.; esp. of Christian doctrine, Ga 2:5, al.; ἀ. θεοῦ, Ro 15:8.
2. Subjectively, truthfulness, truth, not merely verbal (cl.), but sincerity and integrity of character: Jo 8:44, III Jo 3.
3. In phrases (MM, VGT, s.v.): ἐπ’ ἀληθείας, Mk 12:14, al.; ἀ. λέγειν (εἰπεῖν, λαλεῖν), Ro 9:1, II Co 12:6, Eph 4:25, al.; ἀ. ποιεῖν, Jo 3:21, I Jo 1:6 (cf. DB, iv, 818b, ff.).

ἀλλήλων.kj: each other, mutual, one another, (the other), (them-, your-)selves, (selves) together (sometimes with G3326 (μετά) or G4314 (πρός))
ἀλλήλων.as:
ἀλλήλων (gen. pl.), dat. -οις, -αις, acc. -ους, -ας, -α (no nom.), recipr. pron.
(< ἄλλος),
of one another, mutually: Mt 25:32, Mk 4:41, Jo 13:22, al.

ἀλήθω.as:
† ἀλήθω
(κοινή form of the Attic ἀλέω), [in LXX for טחן;]
to grind: Mt 24:41, Lk 17:35.†

ἀλάβαστρον.long: a phial or bottle of perfumed ointment, usually of alabaster.
ἀλάβαστρον.sd: properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material)
ἀλάβαστρον.der: neuter of (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone;
ἀλάβαστρον.as:
ἀλάβαστρον, -ου, τό (also -ος, ὁ, ἡ; colloq. and κοινή for ἀλάβαστος),
[in LXX: IV Ki 21:13 (צַלַּחַת)*;]
a box of alabaster (ἀλαβαστίτης) for ointment: Mt 26:7, Mk 14:3, Lk 7:37 (v. DCG, i, 41b; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀλέκτωρ.as:
ἀλέκτωρ, -ορος, ὁ
(poët. form of ἀλεκτρυών; v. MM, VGT, s.v.), [in LXX: Pr 30:31) (זַרְזִיר; BDB, Lex., 267)*;]
a cock: Mt 26:34, Mk 14:30, 6814:72Lk 22:34, 60, 61, Jo 13:3818:27.†

ἅλυσις.as:
** ἅλυσις, -εως, ἡ,
[in LXX: Wi 17:17*;]
a chain, bond: Mk 5:3, 4, Lk 8:29, Ac 12:6, 721:3328:20, Eph 6:20, II Ti 1:16, Re 20:1.†

ἀλαλάζω.g: I cry aloud, a clanging or clashing cymbal
ἀλαλάζω.long: I cry aloud, raise a war-cry; a clanging or clashing cymbal.
ἀλαλάζω.sd: to vociferate, i.e. (by implication) to wail; figuratively, to clang
ἀλαλάζω.as:
ἀλαλάζω
(onomat. from the battle-cry ἀλαλά), [in LXX chiefly for רוּעַ hi., יָלַל;]
prop, to raise a war-cry, shout with triumph or joy; rarely of grief, to wail: Mk 5:38 (cf. Je 4:8); of a cymbal, ἀλαλάζον (RV. clanging), I Co 13:1 (cf. ὀλολύζω).†

ἄλαλος.long: unable to speak or articulate; speechless.
ἄλαλος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2980 (λαλέω);
ἄλαλος.as:
ἄ-λαλος, -ον
(< λάλος, talkative), [in LXX: Ps 31:18 (אָלַם ni.) Ps 38:13 (אִלֵּם)*;]
dumb, speechless: Mk 7:379:17, 25.†

ἀλεκτοροφωνία.long: the cockcrow, as a period of time, between midnight and 3 a.m.
ἀλεκτοροφωνία.as:
† ἀλεκτοροφωνία, -ας, ἡ
(< ἀλέκτωρ, φωνή),
cock-crowing, i.e. the third watch in the night: Mk 13:35.†

ἀλάβαστρος.long: a phial or bottle of perfumed ointment, usually of alabaster.
ἀλάβαστρος.sd: properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material)
ἀλάβαστρος.der: neuter of (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone;
ἀλάβαστρος.as:
ἀλάβαστρον, -ου, τό (also -ος, ὁ, ἡ; colloq. and κοινή for ἀλάβαστος),
[in LXX: IV Ki 21:13 (צַלַּחַת)*;]
a box of alabaster (ἀλαβαστίτης) for ointment: Mt 26:7, Mk 14:3, Lk 7:37 (v. DCG, i, 41b; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

Ἀλέξανδρος.long: Alexander, a name of Greek origin, (a) son of Simon of Cyrene, (b) the High Priest's kinsman, (c) an Ephesian Jew, (d) the coppersmith.
Ἀλέξανδρος.sd: man-defender; Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man
Ἀλέξανδρος.der: from the same as (the first part of) G220 (ἀλέκτωρ) and G435 (ἀνήρ);
Ἀλέξανδρος.as:
Ἀλέξανδρος, -ου, ὁ,
Alexander
1. Son of Simon of Cyrene: Mk 15:21
2. A kinsman of the High Priest: Ac 4:6.
3. A certain Jew: Ac 19:33.
4. A coppersmith: I Ti 1:20.
5. Perh. = 4 (v. Ellic. on I Ti 1:20): II Ti 4:14.†

ἀληθινός.long: true (lit: made of truth), real, genuine.
ἀληθινός.as:
ἀληθινός, -ή, -όν
(< ἀληθής), [in LXX for אֶמֶת;]
true, in the sense of real, ideal, genuine: Lk 16:11Jo 1:94:23, 376:327:288:1615:117:319:35, I Th 1:9, He 8:29:2410:22, I Jo 2:85:20, Re 3:7, 146:1015:316:719:2; = ἀληθής, Re 19:921:522:6 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†
SYN.: ἀληθής, q.v

ἀλλογενής.as:
† ἀλλογενής, -ές
(< ἄλλος, γένος), [in LXX chiefly for זוּר, נֵכָר;]
of another race, a foreigner ( = ἀλλόφυλος; Cremer, 150; MM, VGT, s.v.): Lk 17:18.†

ἅλλομαι.long: I leap, leap up; of water: I spring up, bubble up.
ἅλλομαι.der: middle voice of apparently a primary verb;
ἅλλομαι.as:
ἅλλομαι
[in LXX for צָלַח, דָּלַג pi., etc.;]
to leap: Ac 3:814:10; of water, to spring up, Jo 4:14 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀλλαχόθεν.g: from another quarter, by another way
ἀλλαχόθεν.long: from another place, by another way.
ἀλλαχόθεν.as:
** ἀλλαχόθεν
adv.
(< ἀλλος), [in LXX: IV Mac 1:7*;] = ἀλλοθεν (v. MM, VGT, s.v.)
from another place: Jo 10:1.†

ἀλόη.long: aloes, the powdered fragrant aloe wood.
ἀλόη.as:
† ἀλόη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ca 4:14א (אֲהָלִים)*;]
the aloe, aloes (the powder of a fragrant wood): Jo 19:39.†

ἁλιεύω.sd: to be a fisher, i.e. (by implication) to fish
ἁλιεύω.as:
ἁλιεύω
(< ἁλιεύς), [in LXX: Je 16:16 (דִּיג)*;]
to fish: Jo 21:3 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

Ἀλεξανδρεύς.long: an Alexandrian, a native (or resident) of Alexandria in Egypt.
Ἀλεξανδρεύς.sd: an Alexandreian or inhabitant of Alexandria

ἀλλάσσω.as:
ἀλλάσσω
(< ἄλλος), [in LXX chiefly for חלף, מוּר hi., etc.;]
1. to change: Ac 6:14, Ga 4:20.
2. to transform: I Co 15:51, 52, He 1:12.
3. to exchange: c. acc., seq. ἐν (= בְּ, Ps 106:20) instead of simple gen. (Bl., § 36, 8), Ro 1:23
(cf. ἀπ-, δι-, κατ-, ἀπο-κατ-, μετ-, συν-αλλάσσω; v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀλλόφυλος.long: foreign, of another tribe or race.
ἀλλόφυλος.as:
ἀλλόφυλος, -ον
(ἄλλος, φῦλον, a tribe), [in LXX chiefly for פְּלֶשֶׁת;]
foreign, of another race (MM, VGT, s.v.); as opp. to a Jew, a Gentile: Ac 10:28.†

ἀλίσγημα.long: pollution, perhaps a polluted thing (especially of food).
ἀλίσγημα.as:
† ἀλίσγημα, -τος, τό
(< late ἀλισγέω, to pollute),
pollution: Ac 15:20.†

ἄλογος.long: without reason, irrational; contrary to reason, absurd.
ἄλογος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3056 (λόγος);
ἄλογος.as:
ἄ-λογος, -ον
[in LXX: Ex 6:12 (שָׂפָהעָרֵל), Nu 6:12 (נָפַל), Jb 11:12, Wi 11:15, 16, IV Mac3*;]
1.without reason, irrational: ζῷα, II Pe 2:12, Ju 10.
2.contrary to reason: Ac 25:27 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

Ἀλεξανδρῖνος.long: Alexandrian, belonging to Alexandria in Egypt.
Ἀλεξανδρῖνος.as:
Ἀλεξανδρινός (Rec. -δρῖνο; v. Kühner3, II, 296), -ή, -όν,
Alexandrian: Ac 27:628:11.†

ἀλαζών.long: a boaster, one who gives one's self airs in a loud and flaunting way.
ἀλαζών.as:
ἀλαζών, -όνος, ὁ, ἡ
(< ἄλη, wandering), [in LXX: Jb 28:8 (שַׁחַץ) Hb 2:5 (יָהִיר), Pr 21:24 (לוּץ)*;]
prop, a vagabond, hence, an impostor, a boaster: Ro 1:30, II Ti 3:2.†
SYN.: ὐβριστής, ὑπερήφανος (v. Tr., Syn., § xxix; Lft., Notes, 256)

ἀλάλητος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2980 (λαλέω);
ἀλάλητος.as:
† ἀ-λάλητος, -ον
(< λαλέω),
inexpressible, not to be uttered: Ro 8:26.†

ἀλοάω.as:
ἀλοάω, -ῶ
(< ἅλως, v.s. ἅλων; and cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), [in LXX chiefly for דּוּשׁ;]
to thresh: I Co 9:99:10; I Ti 5:18.†

ἀληθεύω.g: I say, speak truth, I do truth
ἀληθεύω.long: I say (speak) truth, do truth, maintain truth (the truth).
ἀληθεύω.sd: to be true (in doctrine and profession)
ἀληθεύω.as:
ἀληθεύω
(< ἀληθής), [in LXX: Ge 20:16 (יָכַח) Ge 42:16 (אֶמֶת), Pr 21:3 (מִשְׁפָּט), Is 44:26 (שָׁלַם), Si 34:4*;]
to speak the truth (R, mg., deal truly; Field, Notes, 192): Ga 4:16, Eph 4:15.†

ἀλληγορέω.kj: be an allegory (the Greek word itself)
ἀλληγορέω.as:
*† ἀλληγορέω, -ῶ
(< ἄλλος, ἀγορεύω),
to speak allegorically (Cremer, 96 ff.): Ga 4:24.†

ἀλυπότερος.der: comparative of a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3077 (λύπη);

ἀλυσιτελής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G3081 (λυσιτελεῖ);

ἁλυκός.as:
ἁλυκός, -ή, -όν
(< ἅλς), [in LXX for מֵלַח, שִׂדִּים;]
salt: Ja 3:12.†

ἀλαζονεία.long: boasting, show, arrogant display, ostentation; plur: occasions of ostentation.
ἀλαζονεία.as:
** ἀλαζονία (Rec. -εία, the earlier form), -ας, ἡ
(< ἀλαζών), [in LXX: Wi 5:817:7, 2; IV Mac 5:1-38*;]
the character of an ἀλαζών, boastfulness, vainglory, vaunting: Ja 4:16 (Mayor, in l.), I Jo 2:16.†

ἀλλοτριεπίσκοπος.g: a prier into other men's affairs
ἀλλοτριεπίσκοπος.long: one who meddles in things alien to his calling or in matters belonging to others; factious.
ἀλλοτριεπίσκοπος.sd: overseeing others' affairs, i.e. a meddler (specially, in Gentile customs)
ἀλλοτριεπίσκοπος.as:
* ἀλλοτρι-επίσκοπος (Rec. ἀλλοτριοεπ-), -ου, ὁ
one who meddles in things alien to his calling: I Pe 4:15 (v. ICC, in l.; Deiss., BS, 224-4; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἅλωσις.der: from a collateral form of G138 (αἱρέομαι);
ἅλωσις.as:
ἅλωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< ἁλίσκομαι), [in LXX: Je 50:46 (תּפשׂ ni.)*;]
a taking, capture: II Pe 2:12.†

Ἄλφα.as:
Ἄλφα, τό, indecl. (v.s. Α),
Alpha: Re 1:821:622:13 (v. Swete, in ll.).†

ἁλληλουϊά.sd: praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation
ἁλληλουϊά.der: of Hebrew origin (imperative of H01984 and H03050);
ἁλληλουϊά.as:
† ἁλληλουιά
(Rec. ἀλληλούϊα; Heb.הַלְלוּיָהּ, praise the Lord), [in LXX in the titles of certain Pss (104 (105), al.), and at the end of Ps 150; also To 13:18, III Mac 7:13;]
hallelujah, alleluia: Re 19:1, 3, 419:6.†
